statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 10% (low) after NQZ26 round-tripped its entire overnight advance: the 31,221.25 high failed, roughly 140 points came off, and the contract now prints 31,080.25 to 31,086.50, up only 0.06% to 0.08% against a 31,061.75 prior close and sitting near the 31,059.00 session low. Stress eases to 57% (elevated) as Brent 101.55 and WTI 90.09 press session lows against a Strait of Hormuz that remains effectively closed at Day 218, while ZN December futures hold a 0.16% bid.
recommendation: Tail sits well below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. The narrow danger window spans the 13:00-15:00Z block on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the US cash open, the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z and September ISM Services at 14:00Z, where the published Tail path peaks at 14% on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected.
headline: Tail eases to 10% as the overnight advance fully round-trips and NQ refuses to follow a 2.5% Nikkei melt-up, with crude at session lows holding Stress to 57%
body:
The hour just completed resolved the open question from the previous assessment, and it resolved it in favour of less protection. Two hours ago NQZ26 had extended to a fresh 31,221.25 high and was holding 31,192.00, up 0.42%. The extension failed. Roughly 140 points have since come off, and the contract now prints 31,080.25 on Yahoo Finance at 03:15Z and 31,086.50 on Investing.com at 03:13Z, up 18.50 and 24.75 points against a 31,061.75 prior close, a gain of only 0.06% to 0.08% on 37.72k contracts. The session range is 31,059.00 to 31,221.25, which places current price within about 21 points of the low and roughly 140 points below the high.

That is a complete round-trip of the overnight advance, and it is the single most important observation in this assessment. The prior hour's concern was a shallow-pullback-then-extension sequence, which the contract names explicitly as a Tail amplifier. The sequence has now inverted into its opposite: an extension that failed, followed by a retracement that went the full distance back to the prior close and has not been reabsorbed. Mean reversion did not merely occur, it completed. The private calibration lesson is directly applicable here, which is to let Tail fall quickly when price discovery is orderly and retracements occur. Tail therefore eases three points to 10%, mapping to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal.

The cross-index read confirms rather than complicates this. ES prints 7,775.50, down 1.75 points or 0.02%, on a 7,774.25 to 7,793.00 range and 43.05k contracts. Two hours ago ES was at 7,786.75 and up 0.12%, so the S&P contract has round-tripped alongside the Nasdaq contract and has tipped marginally negative. The 30 basis point NQ-over-ES divergence that characterised the earlier drift has collapsed to roughly 8 basis points. There is no broad risk-seeking path, and there is no longer a narrow tech-led one either.

The decoupling from Asia is the most striking evidence against a pathological path. The Nikkei 225 trades 70,037.61, up 1,728.15 points or 2.53% against a 68,309.46 prior close, sitting at the top of a 69,050.23 to 70,072.13 range; Trading Economics independently shows the index up 2.34% toward 70,000 at a three-month high, led by Advantest, Tokyo Electron and SoftBank. Reuters reports Japanese equities up on easing Fed tightening expectations, with October rate-hike odds priced near 22% against 64% a week earlier, and notes thin conditions with China, South Korea and Australia's New South Wales all closed. A regional melt-up of two and a half percent is producing six to eight basis points in Nasdaq-100 futures. An index that declines to follow that kind of pull, and that gives back its own advance while the pull is still in force, is not exhibiting the directional efficiency that a Tail reading above the low band would require.

Depth remains the reason to hold a small premium above a pure floor rather than cutting further. Mainland China is shut from 1 to 7 October for National Day and reopens on 8 October, Korea is closed, and New South Wales observes a holiday, so price discovery is unusually offshore-driven and the book is thin. Price is also sitting near the session low rather than mid-range, which means a downside extension is the live structural question for the next few hours even though the move so far is an orderly give-back to the prior close rather than a one-way path.

Cross-asset evidence is why Stress eases to 57%. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed on its 218th day, with commercial transit near 1% of the pre-crisis count of roughly 85 vessels per day, war-risk insurance around 40 times normal, eight of the nine largest container carriers suspended or rerouted, and Iran holding to the seven conditions it presented on 25 September. The United States added sanctions on 1 October and is moving the Roosevelt carrier strike group and 2,000 Marines into the region. Against all of that, crude has gone down: Brent is 101.55, off 0.68% against a 102.25 prior close with a 101.31 session low, and WTI is 90.09, off 1.12% with an 89.89 low. Reuters described Brent as steady near 102.20 earlier in the session on Houthi missile reports, so crude has softened since that reporting rather than firmed. Both benchmarks pressing session lows against a declared closure of this duration is an unusually clear statement that Gulf risk is not currently transmitting into equity-index risk.

The standing constraint is unchanged and remains the main component of elevated Stress. Friday's September payroll report missed badly at 29,000 against an 84,000 consensus, unemployment rose to 4.2%, average hourly earnings printed 0.1% on the month and 3.0% on the year, and July was revised to a 10,000 loss with August cut to 133,000. Yields initially fell and then reversed higher into the close, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 4.78%, 5.24% and 5.61% for the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year as of 1 October. The Nasdaq-100 cash index still closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00%, with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31. A record index against a long yield at multi-decade highs is an expensive and difficult environment, which is what 57% Stress inside the elevated band describes, and it has continued to mean-revert. ZN December futures at 104.53, up 0.16% near the top of their range, are the one live piece of relief, easing that tension at the margin without resolving it.

Confidence rises a point to 87%. The evidence base this hour is the densest of the reopen: two independent NQ reads that agree on both the fade and the session extremes, an independent ES read with range and volume, a live ZN read while cash Treasuries are shut, real-time Brent and WTI, two independent Nikkei reads, H.15 constant maturities, the complete September payroll actuals with revisions from a verified report, the confirmed Asian holiday calendar, a full week-ahead US calendar, and the FOMC minutes date independently re-verified at 7 October, 2:00 PM Eastern. The deductions that keep Confidence out of the nineties are unchanged in character: VIX at 15.31 and the cash 10-year are Friday closes rather than live reads, cash Treasuries are shut so the yield tension cannot be confirmed directly, several intended sources returned HTTP 403 or 503 bot-blocks so the Gulf flow strand rests on aggregated reporting whose transit figures remain internally inconsistent, and the shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection time with a partial collection status and two section-level failures, roughly six days stale against the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was treated as unavailable and no breadth, megacap or semiconductor cross-check was folded in.

The published path holds Tail at 10% through Tokyo mid-session, where the thin holiday book remains the channel for any unopposed extension and the 31,059.00 low is the level in question, then decays to a 9% floor as the Asian book is assumed to mature into two-way trade. It ticks to 11% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to the floor through the European morning, and rises into the US session: 13% for the 13:00Z hour containing the cash open and the S&P Global composite and services finals at 13:45Z, both at 58.4 and 58.7 consensus against the same priors, and a 14% session peak for the 14:00Z hour carrying September ISM Services at a 55.0 consensus against 55.7, whose 48.0 employment-component consensus carries particular weight after a 29,000 payroll gain. Both increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances and not assertions that opening or post-release continuation has been observed. The path then decays through the afternoon, ticks to 12% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to the floor across the 21:00Z maintenance halt where no continuous price path exists to be scored, and holds 10% across the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour stays in the low band and maps to EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history. Tail was held at 3% from 03:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Tail then rose through the reopen as the overnight drift extended and a shallow pullback was absorbed: 12% in the 22:00Z slot, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October, before easing to 13% at 02:00Z once a fresh high failed. Stress climbed from 75% at 03:00Z to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, eased through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings into the 14:00Z trough as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and settled at 66%, 65%, 64%, 62% and 60% across the five reopen hours. Confidence ran a narrow 83% to 88% band, peaking in the European and early US hours when verified evidence was densest and easing into the thin weekend and reopen hours.
